summary: Tested the retry-payment flow on /my-orders (Sifarişlərim). Registered a new customer via inline checkout (phone 553062775), closed the initial Epoint iframe to leave the order in 'pending_payment' status, then navigated to /my-orders, expanded the order, and clicked 'Yenidən Ödə'. The frontend fires POST /api/epoint/create-payment as expected (no more window.location.href full-page redirect via startEpointPayment — sanity check: startEpointPayment is not referenced anywhere in MyOrdersPage.tsx anymore). HOWEVER, the retry ALWAYS fails end-to-end because Epoint returns status=error with message 'Duplicate order_id value' since the same order_id (Firestore doc id) was already used in the initial create-payment call. Because getEpointRedirectUrl throws on non-success, setRetryWidgetUrl(url) is never called, the iframe overlay (retry-epoint-widget / retry-epoint-iframe / retry-epoint-close / retry-epoint-skeleton) NEVER renders, and the user just sees an alert('Ödəniş başladıla bilmədi: Duplicate order_id value'). Net result from the user's perspective: pressing 'Yenidən Ödə' still does NOT open Epoint — same user-visible bug as before, just with a different failure mode.

critical.issue: Epoint returns {status:'error', redirect_url:null, message:'Duplicate order_id value'} when the same Firestore order.id is submitted a second time (which is exactly what retry does). This makes the retry flow impossible to complete.

ui_bugs.issue: Sends the same order.id to Epoint on retry. Must generate a unique per-attempt order_id (e.g. `${order.id}-r${retryCount}` or `${order.id}-${Date.now()}`) while persisting the mapping back to the original Firestore order so the webhook/return handler can still find the right order. Without this change, the iframe overlay (retry-epoint-widget) is unreachable in practice, even though the JSX is correctly wired up.
Uses native alert() to show the Epoint error. Consider using the existing NotificationProvider/toast for consistency with the rest of the app.

integration_issues.issue: POST /api/epoint/create-payment is fired (verified via network monitoring), but response is {status:'error', message:'Duplicate order_id value'}. Because getEpointRedirectUrl throws, setRetryWidgetUrl never runs, so retry-epoint-widget / retry-epoint-iframe / retry-epoint-close / retry-epoint-skeleton are never mounted. The user cannot complete the retry.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix handleRetryPayment in /app/src/pages/MyOrdersPage.tsx to send a UNIQUE order_id to Epoint on each retry (e.g. `${order.id}-r${(order.retryCount||0)+1}` or append Date.now()). Keep a mapping (retryOrderId -> original order.id) either as a Firestore field on the order (paymentAttemptIds: string[]) or via prefix parsing so the Epoint webhook / /payment/success handler still resolves the correct order document.
Verify the Epoint result_url / redirect handler correctly resolves the original order.id when it receives the suffixed order_id back.
Consider also updating CartPage's initial submit code path to use the same unique-per-attempt id, so that a user who closes the iframe and then retries via /my-orders is consistent.
Replace alert() with the app's toast/notification component for the error path.
critical_code_review_comments: The iframe overlay JSX in MyOrdersPage.tsx (lines ~967-1030) is correctly mirroring the CartPage pattern with all four testids (retry-epoint-widget, retry-epoint-iframe, retry-epoint-close, retry-epoint-skeleton) — the presentation-layer fix itself is correct.
SANITY CHECK PASSED: `startEpointPayment` is NOT referenced anywhere in MyOrdersPage.tsx. Only `getEpointRedirectUrl` is imported (line 35) and used (line 311). ✓

The real bug is one layer deeper — Epoint's server enforces uniqueness on order_id, but the app reuses the same Firestore doc id on every attempt. This iteration's fix addressed the wrong layer (embedded-iframe blockability) while the actual failure mode in this environment is a business-level rejection from Epoint.
sessionStorage.setItem('pending_epoint_order_id', order.id) is set BEFORE the fetch — good for correlation on return, but the retry-order-id mapping (see action item) needs the same care.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: Epoint uniquely tracks the order_id field. The initial checkout call already registered orderId=<firestoreDocId> with Epoint. When the retry endpoint is called with the same order_id, Epoint rejects with 'Duplicate order_id value'. REPRO: (1) register via checkout, (2) close inline-epoint-close without paying, (3) navigate to /my-orders, (4) expand the pending order, (5) click retry-payment-btn — observe POST /api/epoint/create-payment returns {status:'error', message:'Duplicate order_id value'} and console error 'Retry payment error: Error: Duplicate order_id value'. MITIGATION: send a unique suffixed order_id per attempt (e.g. `${orderId}-r${attemptNo}` or append Date.now()); store attempt count on the Firestore order; strip suffix on webhook return to resolve the original doc.
